title: Type 1 Diabetes in Adults: Newly Diagnosed Pathway

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes: clinical diagnosis, basal-bolus insulin regimen, HbA1c and glucose targets, monitoring, ketones and sick-day rules, hypoglycaemia, education and complication screening, using NICE NG17.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG17 as extracted gives no insulin doses, glucose doses or glucagon doses; insulin starting doses, titration and hypoglycaemia treatment doses must come from the hospital diabetes protocol and the product information.
Sick-day rule details and the diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) treatment protocol were not captured.
HbA1c figures are given in the source in mmol/mol; the Saudi diabetes society targets and unit conventions were not checked.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Type 1 diabetes in adults is diagnosed on clinical grounds in people presenting with hyperglycaemia; age or body mass index (BMI) alone must not exclude or diagnose it. NICE does not routinely measure serum C-peptide to confirm type 1 diabetes in adults. Multiple daily injection basal-bolus insulin is the regimen of choice; non-basal-bolus regimens are not offered to newly diagnosed adults. Rapid-acting insulin analogues are injected before meals and twice-daily insulin detemir is the first-offered basal insulin.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose clinically
actions: Diagnose on clinical grounds; do not use age or BMI alone; do not routinely measure C-peptide.

clinicalManagement.title: Start basal-bolus insulin
actions: Offer multiple daily injection basal-bolus insulin with twice-daily insulin detemir and pre-meal rapid-acting analogue; alternatives are once-daily glargine or degludec under conditions.

clinicalManagement.title: Set monitoring
actions: Offer real-time or intermittently scanned CGM by preference; otherwise test capillary glucose at least 4 times daily; HbA1c every 3 to 6 months.

clinicalManagement.title: Education and sick-day rules
clinicalManagement.timeframe: 6 to 12 months after diagnosis for structured education
actions: Offer a structured education programme 6 to 12 months after diagnosis; give sick-day rules and consider ketone monitoring.

clinicalManagement.title: Screen for complications
actions: Refer to eye screening at diagnosis; yearly albumin:creatinine ratio, eGFR, blood pressure, lipids and TSH.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG17 names insulin detemir, glargine and degludec as basal insulins and rapid-acting analogues before meals but, as extracted, gives no doses. Metformin may be considered off-label for adults with BMI of 25 kg/m2 or above (23 kg/m2 or above for South Asian backgrounds) wanting better control with less insulin, without dose in the source. Intramuscular glucagon and fast-acting oral glucose are named for hypoglycaemia without doses. Follow the hospital diabetes protocol. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) or lower; services report the proportion at 53 mmol/mol (7%) or lower.
5 to 7 mmol/litre; 4 to 7 mmol/litre before meals.
At least 4 times a day including before each meal and before bed.
HbA1c 58 mmol/mol (7.5%) or more or disabling hypoglycaemia despite best management.
